thread:
Alyssa: heads-up — canary stack for kernel-selector v2 caused two OOMs in the last hour on p3.8x (long-context chat workload). repro snippet attached, nvprof snapshot below.

Vikram: ugh. saw something similar earlier when we switched the attention kernel to strided-fused. did you see freelist blow up or just total allocation spike?

Alyssa: total alloc spike + freelist fragmentation. log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-18T10:12:03Z] AllocRequest: 1.2GiB for logits_scratchpad
[2026-03-18T10:12:03Z] Freelist: returned block 256KiB, left 3 holes
[2026-03-18T10:12:04Z] OOM: cannot allocate 512MiB workspace for kv_prefetch
```

Vikram: that pattern smells like we ended up increasing per-item workspace when the new kernel chooses a larger tile size. kernel selection can increase per-layer temporary buffers.

Juan: quick numbers from canary run: baseline kernel v1 avg per-request gpu mem 9.6GB, v2 jumps to 11.8GB (+23%). throughput roughly same but p90 latency +12ms. nvprof summary: 
```
GPU Memory usage (sample): 12444 MiB resident, 384 MiB free, 0.3 GiB fragmentation holes
Top allocations: activations 6.2GB, logits_scratch 2.1GB, kv_cache_warm 1.9GB
```

Maria: KV cache warmed prefixes are big for this workload. if kernel v2 increases scratchpad, combined with an eager kv prefetch we hit the ceiling. two quick mitigations: 1) cap per-request scratchpad via workspace cap, 2) make KV prefetch lazy on oversubscribed hosts.

Alyssa: tried workspace cap at 256MiB per-request, that avoided OOM but degraded p95 by ~18% for long sequences. current tradeoff is latency vs reliability.

Ethan: thoughts: we should prioritize graceful degradation first — automatically fall back to compact kernel when available memory < threshold. also try freelist compaction on allocation bursts (coalesce holes every N allocs). small experiment outline:
- metric: OOM rate, p95 latency, cost tokens/sec
- knobs: workspace_cap {128,256,512}MiB, freelist_compact_freq {0,50,200}, kernel_fallback_threshold {0.7,0.8}

Vikram: agree. implementation notes: freelist compaction is cheap if we run on allocation path tail but must avoid stopping the serving thread. add background compactor on a low-priority cuda stream. compaction heuristic: if free_total < requested and fragmentation_ratio > 0.25, trigger.

Juan: i ran a small AB with compaction freq 50 + workspace_cap 256MiB: OOMs dropped to 0/1200 requests, p95 up +9ms. but GPU util dropped 4%. attaching short flame summary from tensor-profiler.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 2187654401 for kernel-selector v2 started on p3.8x cluster-9 by Alyssa. status: partial success, 2 failed hosts.

Maria: related note — logits buffer reuse isn't fully implemented for v2 because tile sizes changed. we should add a shape-normalized pool for logits/activation buffers: pool key = (dtype, max_elements_bucketed_by_pow2). that reduces fragmentation vs exact-shape freelist.

Alyssa: that pool idea makes sense. i can prototype a pow2-bucketed logits pool. quick config sketch I used: 
```json
{"allocator": "pooled",
 "buckets": [65536, 262144, 1048576],
 "eviction_policy": "lru",
 "per_request_cap": "256MiB"}
```

Ethan: add test where we force different sequence lengths to validate bucket hit-rate. target hit-rate > 85% otherwise buckets too coarse.

Vikram: final concern — make sure kernel fallback decision accounts for batched packing heuristics. sometimes a large batch has slack that masks per-item scratchpad increases; fallback only on host-level free memory rather than per-request.

Alyssa: agreed. next steps: (1) Alyssa prototype pow2 logits pool + background compactor, (2) run grid of knobs Juan suggested, (3) Maria add lazy kv prefetch toggle for canary. i'll push a canary by EOD.

Juan: i'll prepare profiling harness and add nvprof traces for the grid.

Maria: i'll add config flag to route kv prefetch through runtime policy.

Ethan: i'll own the A/B metric dashboard and add OOM alerting.

Alyssa: thanks team :thumbsup: we'll sync in the perf huddle tomorrow.
